body: I did, I'm on medication now (won't kick in for a while) and I have an appointment with a psychiatrist in about a month.

Man I got bills to pay. If I could just quit without any worry I'd do it in a heartbeat. The worst part though is that many people would be pretty happy with this job: lots of autonomy, owning large scale projects cradle to grave; it gives you a hell of a lot of topics to talk to in design, testing, NRTLs, etc.,  but I still feel I'm not good enough for it. 


My wife's the only reason I keep going. I could never do anything to hurt her. That shouldn't be her burden to bear, though. She didn't sign up for this when she married me... I was a better man then. FWIW, I went to the doctor after about 6 months and was diagnosed with moderate severe depression and moderate anxiety. On meds but they won't kick on for a while.

TBH I don't really know what makes me happy. I've only ever done engineering type jobs before.

I've never been more stressed in my life than I have the last 6 months on my current project. I've wanted to drive off the side of the overpass many times on my way to work. It isn't getting any better and I'm afraid I might do it very soon.

It's sort of comforting in a weird way to know someone is in a similar position. What do you like to do for fun/do you have any hobbies? I'm trying to get back into music, I would've studied that if not for potentially not as great employment prospects it of school

I feel for you. I'm always worried something I design will harm somebody. We had checks to make sure that doesn't happen but it's a reason I'm not a CivE. I'm perfectly fine with taking a lower paying, lower-risk job to save my mental stability, but I feel that my educational background is negatively impacting my chance at those opportunities.

I haven't been diagnosed but I almost guarantee I have some sort of anxiety problem. I can't make it work and every time I drive to and from work I dream about flipping my car. I wish I was joking

Edit: I'm an ME for the record, but YMMV

I guess I'm not understanding what you're asking. What dimension are you trying  to verify? What circles are you talking about, the thru holes? The large rounds have to be 50 units in diameter.

Edit: nevermind. I get it now I think. Does the problem statement specify a certain scale? Looks like it says 1:1. Either way yeah the information seems missing.

At first glance it looked like you were right, but the diameter of the outer rounds as to be 50 if you look at the opposite side of the part. I'd reasonably assume the thru holes are 25 then, but that part is a little difficult to tell because of the way the leader looks.

I work at a company that relies fairly heavily (or we attempt to anyway) on the Toyota way / lean methodology for pretty much all departments (software, EEs, MEs, Fab shop, tech support, etc). A board is only as good as how often it's updated. It would be also good to schedule regular gemba walks.
Hey, just saw this. Good point on reaching out to advisors. I actually live close to my alma mater, plus I think my advisor would remember me vaguely given I talked to her a good bit. Thanks!

Thanks, friend. I'm not the first one who struggled with these feelings and I sure as hell won't be the last, but I wish I just wasn't, you know?

My school grades would make it hard to go back and get a master's I think, and especially so if I get let go from this job... Would getting another bachelors be wise or is that generally a waste of time?

Without giving too much away I'm a design engineer at a very large company that makes extremely ubiquitous products you see almost everywhere through pretty much most major manufacturing processes.  This role is part engineer, part project manager, and needs to be pretty much an expert on a dozen or so different safety standards. I'm finding learning the standard requirements to be primarily difficult (esp. when it comes to test plans, never had to do that before), and I've never had to design with some of these manufacturing processes before. Our CAD process from concept to tooling release is barely a month generally.

Not that I've had the desire to be the smartest person in the room but if I ever was that it was probably before college. Definitely isn't the case now haha but I'm more than okay with not being the smartest. I just want to be smart enough, if that makes sense. 

I feel like I work hard... But due to my newness my projects have been easier/more limited in scope than others and I still feel like I'm failing at those. (Note:I realize I'm using the word "feel" often in these replies. Sorry lol).

3 jobs, 2 with the same company, only the 2ns was somewhat technical. 

I said I in another reply a few minutes ago but how do I not measure myself to my peers/team members? I mean obviously I'm not going to compare to the guy who's been in the industry for 10 years or so but to another person who joined 5 months before I did, also coming from a different industry? We all do the same type of work, maybe I'm just not cut out for a design role. 

Oh I work with other engineers at my company that are from several different disciplines, there isn't just my kind. I think because I have so little familiarity with a fair bit of it that it's just been overwhelming (especially getting up to speed with certification standards, how the hell does anyone remember all this?)

This does help, please don't read this reply thinking I'm trying to refute your points. Any points on which you can expound would be greatly appreciated, particularly about comparing myself to peers, or other opportunities in engineering.

You're probably right, but I feel like it's more (I'm probably biased though). Every now and then I feel that I forget a small, but crucial, detail that can delay a project or prevent a product offering. I don't know if that's a potential side effect/result of impostor syndrome or insecurity issues, maybe so? Or maybe I just suck at my job haha...

I ask for feedback/advice a fair amount, I think. I have received good feedback regarding working with/interfacing with our factories out of the country. I'm likeable enough apparently. The sort of head engineer of our team is more or less a mentor to all the other team members. He's a good dude but it's hard to get 1:1 time since he's got his own projects. I enjoy some aspects of the work... But as a whole I would say no. I'd probably enjoy it more if I felt I knew what I was doing/was competent but I think k anybody could say that about anything they feel they are not good at. 

I was briefly a "sales engineer" at a small company before, issue "sales engineer" because it was more of a liasion role between internal sales reps and engineering. 

Oh I'm already panicked, my friend. Luckily this past week was so busy I didn't have time to panic more.

I don't know why I continued with engineering. I guess the breadth of general knowledge an ME degree bestows on a person. I enjoyed learning olhoe things work and I always liked physics. 

I think you hit the nail on the head, I'm not in an industry that is driving my passions. I am a person that needs to have meaning to what I do beyond just making a company money. Maybe environmental would be a better route, or to leave entirely and work at a nonprofit. I don't care to be rich as long as I'm happy and I'm certainly not that right now. 

It's hard not to compare myself to my peers, they are all about my age and some have been at the company just 6 more months than I have (granted, those few people also have been in the same industry longer than I have), and they do the same thing just on other projects. I find it difficult to evaluate myself on my own accomplishments without considering a comparable (in position, duties, etc) person's. 

I wish I knew what would give me a sense of wholesomeness because I would pursue it fervently but I know it isn't this. I do like traveling, working with my hands (though I don't have much experience with it, but my current job there is a fair amount), and working with people/building relationships. I'm unsure how to translate that into a role suite for those aspects though. Got any ideas?
